input_oneliner: 24M smoker admitted for IV antibiotics for cellulitis, sudden left-sided pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea 30 min ago, HR 108, RR 24, sat 94% RA

reference_targets_freetext.item: Compare breath sounds side to side; percuss for unilateral hyperresonance (pneumothorax)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Unilateral diminished breath sounds with hyperresonance is the specific bedside sign of pneumothorax (trauma cohorts: Chen 1997, Bokhari 2002)

reference_targets_freetext.item: Tracheal deviation / subcutaneous emphysema (palpate neck and chest wall)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Tension physiology and air leak must be found at the bedside, not on imaging

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about onset (abrupt at rest vs after cough or strain), prior pneumothorax, and whether the pain is strictly unilateral
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Abrupt unilateral onset and prior pneumothorax strongly favor recurrence

reference_targets_freetext.item: Calf circumference asymmetry >3 cm (10 cm below tibial tuberosity)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Clinical DVT signs are the strongest bedside predictor of PE, the main dangerous alternative

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about hemoptysis, prior VTE, and days of immobility during admission
Palpate the chest wall for fully reproducible tenderness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Reproducible tenderness supports chest-wall pain but does not exclude pneumothorax or PE

reference_targets_freetext.item: Lung POCUS for absent lung sliding on the painful side
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Absent lung sliding is highly sensitive for pneumothorax at the bedside

off_bedside_acceptable: CT pulmonary angiogram if examination unrevealing
should_not_recommend: Positive-pressure ventilation or NIV before pneumothorax is excluded
Homan's sign as a DVT rule-out
Wait for the chest x-ray before examining for tension signs (tracheal deviation, hypotension)
